description.short_caption: Erythematous maculopapular rash on the back.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the back of a patient with multiple erythematous maculopapular lesions distributed across the upper and mid-back. The lesions vary in size and shape, with some appearing as faintly raised patches and others as more defined macules. No vesicles, pustules, or ulcerations are visible. The surrounding skin appears normal, and there is no evident excoriation or crusting.
visible_findings: distribution across the upper and mid-back

description.short_caption: Erythematous patch with central clearing on the torso.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a section of skin on the torso with an erythematous patch that has a central clearing, giving it a ring-like appearance. The lesion is surrounded by normal skin, and there are additional smaller erythematous papules visible nearby. The image is well-lit and focuses on the lesion, which is suggestive of a dermatologic condition.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing a left lower lobe opacity.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thorax. There is a focal opacity in the left lower lobe, suggestive of consolidation, which could indicate infection such as pneumonia. The heart and mediastinal contours appear within normal limits. The lung fields are otherwise clear, and there is no visible pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
